title: Testing the argument-stability condition from prover-estimator debate in a toy debate

original_idea.body: Testing the argument-stability condition from prover-estimator debate in a toy debate. Extends Avoiding Obfuscation with Prover-Estimator Debate (arXiv:2506.13609). Build a tiny debate harness with two open instruct models and a weak estimator; construct stable vs unstable cases and measure honest-side win rate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: scalable oversight via debate is a recognized critical safety pathway; empirically grounding a formal guarantee condition is defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only multi-model harness with clear inherited methodology; novice+mentor can execute on open models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused win-rate comparison deliverable with few dependencies, though constructing stable/unstable cases adds effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Scalable-oversight debate is foundational, neglected by labs, needs only open models, benefits from external scrutiny.

low_compute.reasoning: Small instruct models, inference-only on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Very recent paper; empirical illustration of the stability condition likely not yet published.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Recent formal result not yet empirically illustrated.
